# In page message

Figma: `in page message`, node `548:22140` (page Components, `1:28`).
10 variants - `property 1[5]` x `importance[2]`.

A banner sitting in the page flow. Five severities, two importance levels.

## Markup

```html
<div class="v27-message v27-message--info" role="status">
  <svg class="v27-message__icon" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true"><!-- glyph --></svg>
  <div class="v27-message__body">
    <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

Subtle is applied *alongside* the severity, not instead of it:

```html
<div class="v27-message v27-message--negative v27-message--subtle" role="alert">
  <svg class="v27-message__icon" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true"><!-- glyph --></svg>
  <div class="v27-message__body"><p>Something went wrong.</p></div>
</div>
```

Use `role="alert"` for negative and `role="status"` otherwise.

## The two importance levels differ structurally

Not a shade apart:

| | Bold | Subtle |
|---|---|---|
| background | the severity's own | `Background/Primary` |
| border | the severity's own | `Border/default` |
| text | the severity's own | `Foreground/Primary` |

On Subtle the **icon is the only thing carrying the severity**, which is why the CSS gives
the icon back its type colour rather than letting it inherit.

That has an accessibility consequence worth stating: on Subtle, severity is communicated by
icon colour alone. The glyph itself must differ per severity - do not ship five identically
shaped icons in five colours.

## Values

Geometry verified on `548:22135` (info, Bold) and `7533:8907` (info, Subtle) - identical.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| padding | `--v27-spacing-sm` `--v27-spacing-m` (12px 16px) |
| gap | `--v27-spacing-s` (8px) |
| radius | `--v27-radius-m` (8px) |
| icon | `--v27-size-s` (20px) |
| type | Sm - Outfit 14 / 400 / 16px |

Figma fixes the height at **56px**. The code uses `min-height` instead: a fixed height
clips the second line, and the component's own placeholder copy is long enough to wrap.
This is the one deliberate departure from Figma in the library - FINDINGS.md #20.
